ec.name: Energy code check
ec.notice: A guide for the designer, not a compliance document. It compares what you state with the code's prescriptive package and mandatory minimums. It does not produce a certificate of compliance, and it checks the building envelope only. The energy consultant and the building department decide what complies.
ec.pack: Code: {name}. Numbers read from the authority's documents on {checked}.
ec.cfa.model: From the model: the area inside the outside faces of the exterior walls. Type your own figure if part of that is not conditioned.
ec.zone.ask: Type the site's ZIP code to find its climate zone.
ec.zone.unknown: {code} is not in the code's list of ZIP codes.
ec.walls.intro: The model knows a wall's layers but not what is in the stud cavity. Say what is installed, and the U-factor is read from the code's own table of wall assemblies.
ec.walls.none: The model has no wall of an exterior wall type.
ec.u.give: Use U {si} W/m²K in the heat loss
ec.u.give.all: Use these U-factors in the heat loss ({n} wall types)
ec.u.note: This writes the code table's U-factor, in W/m²K, into the exterior walls of that type (one undo step). Heating and cooling loads read it before the wall's layers, which count a stud layer as solid wood and so make an insulated frame wall leak far too much. It is the table's whole-wall figure, not a calculation of ours. The ceiling and a raised floor have their own buttons below.
ec.u.done.one: {name}: U {si} W/m²K ({u} Btu/h·ft²·°F) written to {n} walls.
ec.u.failed: The U-factor could not be written: {why}
ec.f.ceiling.kind: What is above the top ceiling
ec.ceiling.attic-c: Vented attic, ducts in conditioned space (Option C)
ec.ceiling.attic-b: Vented attic, insulation below the roof deck (Option B)
ec.floor.raised: Raised wood floor over a crawl space
ec.windows.sum: {n} windows in outside walls: {ft} sq ft ({m} m²) of glass, {west} sq ft of it facing west.
ec.windows.none: The model has no window in an exterior wall.
ec.windows.nonorth: The model's site has no latitude and longitude, so true north is not known and the west-facing area cannot be worked out.
ec.windows.rated: The rated values on the window's label. Used for every window that carries none of its own in the model.
ec.counts: {ok} meet the code's figure, {bad} do not, {note} could not be checked.
ec.kept.drawing: What you state here is kept in the drawing, so it travels with the file.
ec.kept.browser: What you state here is kept in this browser.
ec.bim.u.label: Wall U-factor from the energy code
ec.perf.what: The other way to comply is the performance approach (Section {section}): the whole house is simulated and must stay within the standard design's budgets for: {budgets}.
ec.perf.software: Only software the Energy Commission has approved may do that ({section}). The Commission's own program is {software}; the others are on its list.
ec.perf.not: This add-on does not work out those budgets and cannot produce a certificate of compliance.

ec.row.wall.u.mandatory.bad: {name}: U-factor {have} is over the mandatory {need} for {framing} framing. This applies on every compliance path.

ec.row.ceiling.r.bad: Ceiling insulation R-{have} is under the package's R-{need}.
ec.row.ceiling.r.mandatory.ok: Ceiling insulation R-{have} meets the mandatory R-{need}.
ec.row.ceiling.r.mandatory.bad: Ceiling insulation R-{have} is under the mandatory R-{need}. This applies on every compliance path.

ec.row.ceiling.radiant.bad: A radiant barrier is required in this zone, and there is none.
ec.row.ceiling.radiant.q: A radiant barrier is required in this zone.
ec.row.ceiling.below_deck.q: Option B also asks for R-{need} insulation below the roof deck in this zone.

ec.row.floor.r.bad: Raised floor insulation R-{have} is under the package's R-{need}.
ec.row.floor.slab.ok: Slab edge insulation R-{have} meets the package's R-{need}.
ec.row.floor.slab.bad: Slab edge insulation R-{have} is under the package's R-{need}.
ec.row.floor.slab.q: The package asks for R-{need} slab edge insulation in this zone.
ec.row.none.floor.slab: The package has no slab edge insulation requirement in this zone.

ec.row.fen.u.bad: Windows: the area-weighted U-factor {have} is over the package's {need}.
ec.row.fen.u.mandatory.ok: Windows: the area-weighted U-factor {have} is within the mandatory {need}.
ec.row.fen.u.mandatory.bad: Windows: the area-weighted U-factor {have} is over the mandatory {need}. This applies on every compliance path.
ec.row.fen.shgc.ok: Windows: the area-weighted SHGC {have} is within the package's {need}.
ec.row.fen.shgc.bad: Windows: the area-weighted SHGC {have} is over the package's {need}.

ec.row.none.fen.shgc: Windows: the package has no SHGC requirement in this zone.

ec.row.fen.west.bad: West-facing window area is {have} % of the floor area, over the package's {need} %. Less west-facing glass is needed, or the performance path.

ec.row.door.u.bad: Doors: the area-weighted U-factor {have} is over the package's {need}.
ec.row.door.u.q: Doors: the package asks for a U-factor of {need} or less.
ec.row.other.qii.q: Quality insulation installation, verified by a rater, is part of the package.
ec.row.other.fan.q: A whole-house fan is part of the package in this zone.
ec.row.other.roofing.q: Steep-slope roofing with an aged solar reflectance of {need} and a thermal emittance of {emittance} is part of the package in this zone.
ec.row.other.systems.q: Heating, cooling, ducts, water heating, ventilation, solar panels and the battery-ready rules are part of the package too.
ec.row.zone.q: The climate zone is not known.
ec.why.cavity: Say what is between the studs.
ec.why.table-row: The code's table has no row for that combination.
ec.why.table-spacing: The code's table has no values for that spacing.
ec.why.table-no-table: This code pack has no wall table.
ec.why.none: There is nothing in the model to check.
ec.why.not-checked: This add-on does not check it.
ec.why.cfa: The conditioned floor area is needed.
ec.why.bearing: True north is not known, so which windows face west cannot be told.
ec.cbecc.h: A project file for the approved program
ec.cbecc.what: Saves the building envelope as a project file (.ribd25) for {program}, the Energy Commission's own compliance program, so the energy consultant starts from your model and not from a blank form: the climate zone, the conditioned floor area, each outside wall by the direction it faces with its windows and doors, the ceiling, the attic, the floor and their constructions.
ec.cbecc.missing: The file cannot be written yet. Still needed:
ec.cbecc.assumed: The file states these things that nobody told it. Check each one in the program:
ec.cbecc.left: Not in the file, for the consultant to add in the program:
ec.cbecc.proof: How far this is proven: every object, property and word in the file is checked against the program's own published data model, and the same check passes the Commission's 24 example houses. We have not opened the file in the program itself. It is a starting file, not a compliance result.
ec.cbecc.saved: Saved {name}. Open it in the program, add the systems, and check what the file assumed.
ec.cbecc.miss.zone: The climate zone: type the site's ZIP code.
ec.cbecc.miss.height: The height of the outside walls.
ec.cbecc.miss.walls: Outside walls of an exterior wall type in the model.
ec.cbecc.miss.north: True north: the model's site needs a latitude and longitude.
ec.cbecc.miss.wall-insulation: For every outside wall type: the stud size and what is between the studs.
ec.cbecc.miss.wall-words: A wall whose studs or insulation the program has no word for.
ec.cbecc.miss.ceiling: What is above the top ceiling.
ec.cbecc.miss.ceiling-kind: Only a vented attic with the ducts in conditioned space (Option C) can be written so far.
ec.cbecc.miss.ceiling-r: The ceiling insulation, as a whole R-value the program lists.
ec.cbecc.miss.floor: The lowest floor: raised or slab.
ec.cbecc.miss.floor-r: The floor insulation, as a whole R-value the program lists.
ec.cbecc.miss.window-sizes: A width, height and direction for every window.
ec.cbecc.miss.perimeter: The length of the outside walls of the lowest level.
ec.cbecc.as.footprint: The ceiling and floor areas are the floor area divided by the number of levels.
ec.cbecc.as.crawl-height: The crawl space walls are 2 ft high and the floor is 2 ft above the ground.
ec.cbecc.as.floor-joists: The floor joists are 2x6 at 16 in. on centre.
ec.cbecc.as.slab-surface: The slab has the program's default covering and no edge insulation.
ec.cbecc.as.roofing: The roofing is asphalt shingle on a wood deck over trusses at 24 in.
ec.cbecc.as.wall-finish: The outside wall finish is siding (a wall type named stucco is written as three-coat stucco).
ec.cbecc.as.radiant: There is no radiant barrier (you did not say).
ec.cbecc.left.systems: Heating, cooling, ducts, water heating and ventilation.
ec.cbecc.left.garage: The garage, if there is one, and the walls between it and the house.
ec.cbecc.left.shading: Overhangs, fins and other shading of the windows.
ec.cbecc.left.run: The street address, the run settings and the report options.
ec.cbecc.view: This file holds areas and directions, not shapes, so a model viewer cannot draw it, and viewers made for the program's nonresidential files will not open it. To look at the same model as a 3D shape in an outside viewer, save the EnergyPlus file instead: Energy tab, Check with EnergyPlus, Save.
ec.ceiling.u.cathedral: The pack has no table for a cathedral (rafter) ceiling, so no U-factor is given for it.
ec.f.floor.heated: Heated slab (pipes or cables in it)
ec.slab.f: Slab F-factor {f} Btu/h·ft·°F per foot of slab edge ({si} W/mK), {table}, page {page}.
ec.slab.fp: Along the lowest level's exterior walls: {fp} Btu/h·°F ({si} W/K).
ec.slab.note: A slab on the ground loses heat through its edge, so the code gives it an F-factor per foot of edge, not a U-factor over its area. It is shown here and not written into the model: the quick heat loss counts a ground floor by its area against the ground temperature, which is a different method.
ec.u.give.roof: Use U {si} W/m²K in the heat loss ({n} roof elements)
ec.u.give.floor: Use U {si} W/m²K in the heat loss ({n} floor slabs, lowest level)
ec.u.env.note: The ceiling button writes the attic table's whole-assembly U-factor into every roof element (IfcRoof and slabs typed as a roof); the floor button writes the raised-floor table's U-factor into the floor slabs of the lowest level. One undo step each. A flat ceiling slab under an attic is not written: give it the figure by hand if the loads stop at it.
ec.u.done.roof: U {si} W/m²K ({u} Btu/h·ft²·°F) written to {n} roof elements.
ec.u.done.floor: U {si} W/m²K ({u} Btu/h·ft²·°F) written to {n} floor slabs.
